rationale: Base station is online with uplink_status "ok", yet E-503 "TLS handshake error" repeats in the logs, meaning events never reach the cloud (hence no push notifications while local siren still works). The standard L1 fix (router + base station power-cycle, DNS set to automatic) was attempted and did not resolve the issue. Per the fault-code reference and historical case H-06, persistent E-503 with TLS handshake failure while the base is online indicates a backend certificate/cloud-channel issue requiring FAE escalation.

complaint: Since last week we don't get any push notifications on our phones, even though the siren works when the alarm goes off at home. I reinstalled the app on both phones and it didn't help. Maybe the latest app version is just buggy? Is there an older version I can install?
usability_reason: The response is polite and clearly summarizes the symptom and suspected cause, and it accurately reflects that the power-cycle/DNS step was performed and did not resolve the issue. However, actionability is weak: it offers no concrete next steps for the customer, no timeline, and does not address the customer's question about an older app version. It also references internal diagnostics (E-503, historical case H-06) without explaining them, and the escalation is vague ('engineering team will investigate'). It avoids overclaiming fixes, which is good, but the customer is left without meaningful guidance.
